Below you are told what you can see and hear around you right now. Say what you do from now on: how you move, and any signal you make.
Left and right always mean your own left and right.
Other people see how you move and any signal you make, if you are in their view. Nobody hears a signal. Nobody else knows your intent or your reason.
You may be asked again later, if something changes.

HOW TO REPLY
Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"signal": a signal you make now with your eyes, head or hands: "none", "eye_contact", "nod", "wave_on", "hold_up_hand", "point" or "other".
"intent": what you are trying to do, in your own words.
"steps": what you do from now on, as a list of steps (see STEPS). Write [] if you carry on as you are.
"reason": why, in your own words. Nobody else sees it.
The format, with placeholders: {"signal": "<a signal, or none>", "intent": "<what you are trying to do>", "steps": [<step>, ...], "reason": "<why>"}

STEPS
The steps are carried out in order, each beginning when the one before it ends, unless it has a start that has not come yet: then it begins when its start comes, and until then you walk on towards where you are going. After the last step ends, you walk on towards where you are going. Each step is a JSON object with these keys; leave out the ones you do not need:
"start": in any step, when it begins: "now", {"at_distance_m": <metres>} to begin when the person you would meet is that close to you, or {"after_seconds": <seconds>}, counted from now. Without it, the opening step begins now and a later step begins when the one before it ends.
"speed_mps": the speed you walk at during the step, in m/s, from 0 (standing still) up to the fastest you can walk.
"turn": {"to": "left" or "right", "degrees": <from 0 to 90>}: during the step, walk at this angle to your left or right of the direction you are going.
"back_up_m": walk backwards this many metres. The step ends when you have.
"until": when the step ends: {"seconds": <seconds>}, {"at_distance_m": <metres>} to end it when the person you would meet is that close to you, or one of these events, written as its name in quotes: "other_passes" (until the other person has passed you), "other_stops" (until the other person stops) or "i_am_out_of_the_stretch" (until you are out of the narrow stretch). Every step needs it, except a step that walks backwards.
The format of a step, with placeholders: {"start": "now", "speed_mps": <number>, "turn": {"to": "<left or right>", "degrees": <number>}, "until": {"seconds": <number>}}

ABOUT YOU
- You are 25 years old.
- You are a woman.
- You are on your way to the supermarket.
- You are walking at 1.30 m/s. Your usual walking speed is 1.30 m/s.
- The fastest you can walk is 2.00 m/s.
- Your body is 0.50 m wide.
- You are Chinese.
- You are easy-going and tend to give way.
- You live in Singapore.

WHERE YOU ARE
- You are in a passage 1.75 m wide. The wall on your left is 1.18 m from you, the wall on your right 0.57 m.
- It is busy and noisy around you.
- It is the middle of the day.

WHO YOU CAN SEE
- Person 1, 4.2 m away, ahead of you and 11° to your left.
  They are walking at 1.00 m/s, in the opposite direction to you, drifting to your right by 25°, and the distance between you is shrinking.
  Their body is 0.50 m wide.
  They look about 70 years old.
  They look like a man.
  They nod at you.
  Since you last looked, they have slowed down.
  They look Chinese.
  They are looking at their phone as they walk.
  You find them attractive.
  You know each other from your classes.

WHAT YOU HAVE DONE SO FAR
- 2.2 s ago you decided: "Keep walking to the supermarket while making room for the older man."
  Since then you have moved 0.4 m over to your right.
  You changed those steps at your next decision.
- 1.2 s ago you decided: "Keep walking to the supermarket and give the older man room to pass, getting his attention so he looks up from his phone"
  You made eye contact.
  Since then you have moved 0.4 m over to your right.
  You are still carrying out those steps.

At your current speeds you would meet Person 1 in about 1.9 s.

Something has changed since you last decided. What do you do now? Your reply replaces whatever is left of your earlier steps. Reply with the JSON object only.

{"signal": "nod", "intent": "Acknowledge him and keep to my right so he can pass safely while he's on his phone", "steps": [{"start": "now", "speed_mps": 1.10, "until": {"at_distance_m": 1.2}}, {"start": {"at_distance_m": 1.2}, "speed_mps": 1.30, "until": "other_passes"}], "reason": "He nodded back but he's still looking at his phone and drifting into my path; slowing a little and holding my right side gives him room to pass without bumping."}

Stepping out of the role now. Earlier, as this person, you:
- decided: "Keep walking to the supermarket while making room for the older man."
  Your steps were: [{"start": {"at_distance_m": 3.0}, "speed_mps": 1.3, "turn": {"to": "right", "degrees": 15.0}, "until": {"at_distance_m": 1.2}}, {"start": {"at_distance_m": 1.2}, "speed_mps": 1.1, "turn": {"to": "left", "degrees": 10.0}, "until": "other_passes"}].
- decided: "Keep walking to the supermarket and give the older man room to pass, getting his attention so he looks up from his phone"
  Your steps were: [{"start": "now", "speed_mps": 1.3, "turn": {"to": "right", "degrees": 15.0}, "until": {"at_distance_m": 2.5}}, {"speed_mps": 1.2, "until": "other_passes"}].
  Your signal was: eye_contact.
- decided: "Acknowledge him and keep to my right so he can pass safely while he's on his phone"
  Your steps were: [{"start": "now", "speed_mps": 1.1, "until": {"at_distance_m": 1.2}}, {"start": {"at_distance_m": 1.2}, "speed_mps": 1.3, "until": "other_passes"}].
  Your signal was: nod.
Was what you did based on anything: a law or official guidance, a published study, a local custom, a habit, or nothing in particular? If you know a specific source, name it. If there is none, say so. That is a perfectly good answer.

HOW TO REPLY
Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys:
"basis": in your own words, what you did was based on.
"kind": one of "law_or_guidance", "published_study", "local_custom", "habit", "common_sense" or "none".
"source": a specific source you know of, as a citation, or "none".
"applies_to": which of your decisions this is about.
The format, with placeholders: {"basis": "<what it was based on>", "kind": "<one of the kinds>", "source": "<a citation, or none>", "applies_to": "<which decision>"}

attempts.raw_output: {"basis": "Just everyday courtesy and self-preservation: giving an elderly person, distracted by his phone, room to pass so we don't bump in a narrow passage. No law, study, or formal custom in mind.", "kind": "common_sense", "source": "none", "applies_to": "All three decisions: making room, getting his attention with eye contact, and nodding while keeping to my right."}
